audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel / Shemuel Bet chapter 2, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Hebron inquiry, household migration, Judah's anointing, Jabesh-gilead messaging, Abner's installation of Ish-bosheth, divided chronology, the Gibeon pool contest, Asahel's pursuit and death, casualty counts, and burial.

verses.restored: After this David inquired of YHWH, saying, Shall I go up into one of cities of Judah? YHWH said to him, Go up. David said, To where shall I go up? YHWH said, To Hebron.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after this, that David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the LORD said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.

verses.restored: David went up there, and also his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

familiar.text: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabal’s wife the Carmelite.

verses.restored: David brought up his men who were with him, each man and his household, and they lived in cities of Hebron.

familiar.text: And his men that were with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.

verses.restored: Men of Judah came and anointed David there as king over house of Judah. They told David, saying, Men of Jabesh-gilead were those who buried Saul.

familiar.text: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, That the men of Jabeshgilead were they that buried Saul.

verses.restored: David sent messengers to men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, Blessed are you to YHWH, because you did this covenant-kindness with your lord, with Saul, and buried him.

familiar.text: And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabeshgilead, and said unto them, Blessed be ye of the LORD, that ye have shewed this kindness unto your lord, even unto Saul, and have buried him.

verses.restored: Now may YHWH do covenant-kindness and faithfulness with you. I also will do this good with you, because you have done this thing.

familiar.text: And now the LORD shew kindness and truth unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.

verses.restored: Now let your hands be strong, and be children of strength, because Saul your lord is dead, and also house of Judah has anointed me king over them.

familiar.text: Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be ye valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.

verses.restored: But Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, took Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim.

familiar.text: But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;

verses.restored: He made him king over Gilead, Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, and over all Israel.

familiar.text: And made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.

verses.restored: Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only house of Judah followed David.

familiar.text: Ishbosheth Saul’s son was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.

verses.restored: Number of days David was king in Hebron over house of Judah was seven years and six months.

familiar.text: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

verses.restored: Abner son of Ner and servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

familiar.text: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

verses.restored: Joab son of Zeruiah and servants of David went out and met them at pool of Gibeon together. These sat on one side of pool, and those sat on other side of pool.

familiar.text: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.

verses.restored: Abner said to Joab, Please let young men arise and play/fight before us. Joab said, Let them arise.

familiar.text: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.

verses.restored: They arose and crossed over by number: twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from servants of David.

familiar.text: Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, which pertained to Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.

verses.restored: Each grasped head of his companion and thrust his sword into side of his companion, and they fell together. Therefore that place was called Field of Sharp Blades, which is in Gibeon.

familiar.text: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkathhazzurim, which is in Gibeon.

verses.restored: Battle was very severe on that day, and Abner and men of Israel were struck before servants of David.

familiar.text: And there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.

verses.restored: Three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was swift in his feet like one gazelle that is in field.

familiar.text: And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.

verses.restored: Asahel pursued after Abner and did not turn to go right or left from after Abner.

familiar.text: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.

verses.restored: Abner turned behind him and said, Is this you, Asahel? He said, It is I.

familiar.text: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Art thou Asahel? And he answered, I am.

verses.restored: Abner said to him, Turn aside to your right or to your left, seize for yourself one of young men, and take his equipment for yourself. But Asahel was not willing to turn aside from after him.

familiar.text: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from following of him.

verses.restored: Abner again said to Asahel, Turn aside from after me. Why should I strike you to ground? How then could I lift my face to Joab your brother?

familiar.text: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?

verses.restored: But he refused to turn aside. Abner struck him in abdomen with rear of spear, and spear came out behind him. He fell there and died in his place. All who came to place where Asahel fell and died stood still.

familiar.text: Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth rib, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.

verses.restored: Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner. Sun was going down when they came to hill of Ammah, which is before Giah by way of wilderness of Gibeon.

familiar.text: Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that lieth before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.

verses.restored: Children of Benjamin gathered after Abner and became one band, and they stood on top of one hill.

familiar.text: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill.

verses.restored: Abner called to Joab and said, Shall sword devour forever? Do you not know that it will be bitter in latter end? How long will you not say to people to return from after their brothers?

familiar.text: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from following their brethren?

verses.restored: Joab said, As Divine lives, if you had not spoken, surely only in morning would people have gone up, each from pursuing his brother.

familiar.text: And Joab said, As God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.

verses.restored: Joab blew shofar, and all people stood still. They no longer pursued after Israel, and they did not continue to fight.

familiar.text: So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.

verses.restored: Abner and his men walked through Arabah all that night, crossed Jordan, walked through all Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.

familiar.text: And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.

verses.restored: Joab returned from after Abner and gathered all people. From servants of David nineteen men were missing, and Asahel.

familiar.text: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.

verses.restored: Servants of David had struck from Benjamin and among men of Abner three hundred sixty men who died.

familiar.text: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner’s men, so that three hundred and threescore men died.

verses.restored: They lifted Asahel and buried him in tomb of his father, which was in Bethlehem. Joab and his men walked all night, and daylight came upon them at Hebron.

familiar.text: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which was in Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.

translation_notes: David's move to Hebron includes wives, soldiers, dependents, and whole households. Political transition is lived by communities, not by a solitary hero.
David's message to Jabesh-gilead honors burial work while also functioning as an appeal to a city loyal to Saul. Piety and political strategy coexist.
Ish-bosheth is installed through Abner's military power. His name may reflect a later shame-substitution for Eshbaal; textual and naming traditions require audit.
The reign lengths and territorial claims create chronological tensions. The data should not be smoothed into false precision.
The pool encounter called 'play' is a lethal staged contest in which twenty-four young men kill one another. It is not sport, entertainment, or a model of honorable masculinity.
Asahel's speed is a bodily trait, not proof of invulnerability or moral superiority. Abner warns him twice before killing him, but battlefield warning does not cleanse the wider civil war.
Casualty imbalance may function as royal propaganda. Every counted death represents a person within a divided people.
Abner's appeal to brotherhood stops the pursuit only after extensive killing. Shared identity should prevent violence earlier, not merely conclude it.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not romanticize the Gibeon contest, civil war, pursuit, or casualty arithmetic. Do not treat providential inquiry as permission for dynastic conquest. Center households, young fighters used by commanders, the dead on both sides, and the political interests behind competing anointings.
